completed: THE LOGGING FIX IS DONE AND PROVEN. main.js wrote six diagnostics through bare console calls that never reached app.log, because main's stdout has no capture (only the fork's, via pipeChildStream). All six now go through the logger main already imports: lines 295 (window state), 639/640 (APP_USER_DATA / APP_DOCUMENTS), 644 (portable roots), 817 (Server signaled ready) and 833 (Server signal timed out). server.js:19 dotenv now passes { quiet: true }. Commit 3cb4a58d.

A SIXTH call was found and swept in the same pass: main.js:295 'Failed to load window state' - same class, same silent hole, and a window-geometry failure is squarely 'the app opened weird' territory. The handoff that preceded this one named only five.

Line 833 was PROVEN, not assumed. A healthy boot can never print it (it is mutually exclusive with 'Server signaled ready'), so the 5000ms fallback was temporarily dropped to 1ms, the app launched, the [WARN] [main] line was caught in the real log, and the edit was reverted. onReady is idempotent (main.js:785) so tripping it early is safe. git diff confirmed 5000 restored before commit.
Build #4 = CI run 30668727944 from 3cb4a58d, all three platforms green. Log confirms 'HEAD is now at 3cb4a58d' and buildHash 3cb4a58d4202.

Build dispatch: gh workflow run cubric-vision-portable.yml --repo MadPonyInteractive/mpi-ci --ref main -f source_repo=MadPonyInteractive/Cubric-Vision -f ref=<FULL 40-CHAR SHA> -f version=1.3.0. ~6 min. A SHORT sha fails at checkout in ~40s. Confirm via 'HEAD is now at' in the run log.
CI gates builds on docs/releases/.approved-1.3.0.json. ANY releaseNotes.js edit stales it. Re-approve with `node scripts/release-notes-approval.mjs approve --yes`.
jq is NOT installed on this machine. Use `gh ... --template` or python for JSON, never jq - a jq-based watcher silently never fires.

Launching the app from Git Bash contaminates PATH: GNU tar 1.35 wins over Windows bsdtar and reads 'D:/...' as a REMOTE HOST ('tar: Cannot connect to D: resolve failed'). It falls back to extract-zip and recovers, so it is NOT a user-facing bug - a user double-clicking from Explorer gets System32 bsdtar. Launch via `explorer.exe <path>` for a faithful test.
scp to the Mac must use the /d/... form, NOT D:/... - scp reads 'D:' as a remote host.
Do NOT extract on the Mac while scp is still writing. Archive Utility reports 'Error 94 - Bad message' on a partial zip and it reads exactly like a corrupt build.
On the Mac, `pkill -f CubricVision` does NOT finish the job - Electron respawns helpers and pgrep also self-matches the ssh command. Kill by PID from `ps -eo pid,command`, then re-count.

MEASURED file formats, do not assume: board.json is CRLF / indent 2 / trailing newline; the ROOT events.jsonl is CRLF; per-task events.jsonl VARY - MPI-413's is CRLF even though older notes claim per-task files are LF. Always measure, and parse-guard before writing.
board.json structure is `columns` as a DICT of name -> [task ids], not a list of column objects.
Shared tree with concurrent agents - commit by explicit pathspec, never git add -A.
Kill agent-spawned processes at the end.
